declaration.preface:
Anupam Rasayan India Limited (ARIL), established in 1984, is committed to promoting sustainability and responsibility across its supply chain. Through this Sustainable and Responsible Procurement Policy, we aim to ensure that all goods and services are sourced ethically, transparently, and with minimal environmental and social impact.

We work collaboratively with our suppliers and business partners to uphold principles of fair trade, human rights, safety, and environmental stewardship, in line with the UN Global Compact, ISO 20400 Sustainable Procurement Guidelines, and BRSR requirements.

This policy reflects ARIL’s belief that responsible procurement strengthens long-term partnerships, supports local communities, and contributes to a more sustainable future.
declaration.declaration: Anupam Rasayan is committed to ensuring that its procurement practices support sustainability, ethical conduct, and social responsibility across the value chain. We aim to partner with suppliers who share our commitment to environmental protection, fair labor practices, and business integrity. Our procurement commitments are defined under the following key focus areas:
declaration.scope:
This Sustainable and Responsible Procurement Policy applies to all Anupam Rasayan India Limited (ARIL) facilities, employees, contractors, and suppliers involved in procurement, logistics, and supply chain operations.

It covers the sourcing of raw materials, packaging materials, equipment, and services across all manufacturing units, R&D facilities, and administrative offices.

The policy extends to vendors, business partners, and third-party service providers, ensuring that all procurement activities are aligned with ARIL’s principles of ethical conduct, environmental responsibility, human rights, and fair labor practices.

Ethical Sourcing: We ensure that all products and services are procured transparently and in compliance with applicable laws, ethical standards, and anti-corruption principles. Suppliers are expected to operate with integrity, avoiding bribery, fraud, and unfair trade practices in all transactions.
Environmental Responsibility: Suppliers must minimize their environmental footprint by adopting sustainable production methods, waste reduction measures, and energy-efficient processes. Preference is given to suppliers that use eco-friendly materials, manage waste responsibly, and work toward carbon reduction.
Labor and Human Rights Standards: All suppliers are required to uphold internationally recognized human rights and fair labor practices. Forced labor, child labor, unsafe working conditions, or any form of discrimination are strictly prohibited within our supply chain.
Health and Safety: Suppliers must maintain a safe and healthy workplace by following relevant safety laws and implementing occupational health programs. ARIL encourages continuous improvement in safety standards across the supply chain.
Local and Inclusive Procurement: We promote local sourcing and inclusion of small, medium, and diverse suppliers where feasible, contributing to regional economic development and community growth.
Supply Chain Transparency: We expect suppliers to provide accurate, traceable information about materials, sourcing practices, and environmental or social impacts. Regular audits and performance evaluations are conducted to ensure compliance with ARIL’s sustainability standards.

targets.target: Sets 2022 as the baseline for tracking progress in sustainable procurement, supplier responsibility, and ethical sourcing across all operations and supply chain partners.
Conduct ESG on-site audits at 100% of operational sites and critical supplier locations by 2027, ensuring comprehensive evaluation of environmental, social, and governance performance.
Deliver annual ESG and sustainability awareness training covering at least 20% of active suppliers by 2027, with progressive increase in coverage each year.
Integrate sustainability performance criteria (covering environmental, labor, ethics, and safety aspects) into 100% of new supplier selection and contract renewals by 2027.
Ensure 100% of procurement employees and decision-makers complete sustainability and responsible sourcing training by 2026.
Increase procurement from sustainable and eco-certified suppliers by at least 25% by 2027, prioritizing those demonstrating measurable ESG improvements.
Ensure 100% of suppliers and contractors comply with ARIL’s Code of Conduct and ethical business requirements by 2027.
Conduct annual anti-corruption and compliance training for 100% of procurement and supply chain teams by 2026.
Perform ethical due diligence assessments for 100% of high-risk suppliers by 2027.
Achieve zero tolerance for corruption, bribery, or unethical practices in all procurement transactions.
Conduct sustainability and environmental risk assessments for 100% of critical suppliers by 2027.
Ensure that at least 30% of suppliers adopt measurable environmental management programs (energy, waste, or water reduction) by 2027.
Prioritize suppliers using eco-friendly packaging and recyclable materials in 20% of procurement by 2027.
Achieve zero non-compliance cases with environmental laws or supplier sustainability requirements.
Achieve 100% supplier compliance with labor and human rights criteria by 2027, including prohibition of child and forced labor.
Conduct social and ethical audits for 100% of Tier-1 suppliers by 2027.
Train 100% of procurement officers and vendor managers on human rights and labor due diligence by 2026.
Report zero instances of supplier-related human rights violations each year.
Conduct annual health and safety compliance audits for 100% of critical suppliers by 2027.
Achieve 100% supplier awareness of ARIL’s EHS (Environment, Health & Safety) requirements by 2026.
Integrate safety performance evaluation into all supplier selection and renewal processes by 2027.
Maintain zero serious injury or fatality cases reported within the supplier network.
Increase local and regional sourcing by 90% by 2027 to strengthen community engagement and reduce logistics emissions.
Engage at least 90% of total suppliers from small, medium, or women-owned enterprises by 2027.
Host annual supplier development programs to build sustainability capacity among local vendors.
Ensure 100% payment transparency and fair terms for all local suppliers.
Implement a Supplier Sustainability Evaluation System covering 100% of suppliers by 2027.
Ensure 100% traceability of critical raw materials to verified and responsible sources by 2027.
Publish annual supplier sustainability performance data in the Sustainability Report starting FY2025–26.
Conduct supplier risk assessments for all new vendors before onboarding.

policy.reviewMechanism:
The Sustainability Committee, in coordination with the Procurement Department, Ethics and Compliance Committee, and EHS Team, shall be responsible for conducting the annual review of this Sustainable and Responsible Procurement Policy.

The review will assess the policy’s effectiveness, supplier performance outcomes, progress on sustainability targets, and alignment with current laws, global standards, and organizational objectives.

It will also evaluate supplier risk assessment results, audit findings, and corrective actions implemented during the reporting period.

Any updates or revisions arising from operational changes, new regulations, audit feedback, or stakeholder inputs will be submitted to the Board of Directors for approval. Once approved, the revised policy will be communicated to all relevant employees, suppliers, and business partners to ensure continued alignment with Anupam Rasayan’s sustainable procurement goals and ESG commitments.
